label: EU-aiact-sandboxes-2026 Article 2

obligations.text: Providers and prospective providers shall have non-discriminatory and transparent access to clear and publicly available information about the scope of the AI regulatory sandbox, and the services offered by the competent authorities within the AI regulatory sandbox.

Access to and participation in an AI regulatory sandbox for SMEs, including start-ups, shall be prioritised and free of charge for services of regulatory guidance, advice and supervision concerning (the compliance with) Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and other Union and national law supervised in the AI regulatory sandbox, including supervision of the testing in real-world conditions, support for conformity assessment, reliance on relevant regulatory privileges in accordance with Article 57(12) and Article 59 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, redirection to pre-deployment services, and supervision of the testing and validating of AI systems.
The AI regulatory sandboxes that may be established by the AI Office shall provide priority access to SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs, pursuant to Article 57(3a) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
Such costs shall concern other services that shall be agreed upon between the competent authority or competent authorities and the participant in the sandbox plan.

The recovery of exceptional costs for other services shall be carried out in a fair, transparent and proportionate manner without prejudice to Member States making use of possibilities foreseen under State aid rules, as applicable.

When charging SMEs, including start-ups, a fee for exceptional costs, the invoice shall be sufficiently detailed in order for the participant to understand which exceptional costs have occurred and how they have been calculated.
Prospective participants shall be informed about the possibility that exceptional costs might be incurred as early as possible and at least before the participation starts.
Public authorities, bodies and agencies shall also benefit from the pricing regime specified in this paragraph.
In such case, competent authorities shall define and publish the list of fees that apply for participation, when opening the application phase pursuant to Article 3.

Providers or prospective providers who do not have a registered office or a branch in the Union and who have been selected following the fulfilment of the eligibility and selection criteria referred to in Article 3(2) and (3) of this Regulation, shall pay to the competent authority a participation fee and include in the application to participate in an AI regulatory sandbox information about the designated authorised representative established in the Union, through a written mandate, who can represent the provider or prospective provider and be held responsible and liable as a guarantee for the compliance of the provider or prospective provider’s activities in the AI regulatory sandbox.
